newsitem.title: FRANCE: French poll gives right wafer-thin majority.
newsitem.headline: French poll gives right wafer-thin majority.

text.p: An opinion poll published on Thursday suggested that France's centre-right government would win only a wafer-thin majority in a snap parliamentary election on May 25 and June 1.

The IPSOS poll for the weekly Le Point, taken on Tuesday and Wednesday, showed the ruling coalition would win 292 seats in the 577-member National Assembly, with the opposition Socialists taking 256, the Communists 28 and the extreme-right National Front 1.
Thirty-one percent of the 1,633 adults questioned in the telephone poll did not state their voting intention.

IPSOS based its projection in seats on the following voting intentions: 39.5 percent for the ruling RPR-UDF coalition, 29 percent for the Socialist party, 15 percent for the National Front, 10 percent for the Communists, five percent for the ecologists and 1.5 percent for the extreme-left.

Compared to the last IPSOS survey in March, the poll found a 0.5 point decline in support for the coalition and a three-point gain for the Socialists, with a similar decline in backing for the ecologists. Support for the National Front and the Communists remained constant.

It was the second poll to be taken since President Jacques Chirac called the election on Monday. A CSA institute survey taken on Tuesday suggested the coalition would win 332 seats, the Socialists 201, the Communists 20 and the National Front one of the 555 seats in metropolitan France.
